choices.misconception: I wrote 8^4 as 2^12 correctly, but I rewrote 4^3 as 2 to the power 2^3 = 2^8 instead of (2^2)^3 = 2^6, so I got 12 + 8 = 20.
I multiplied the bases, 8 times 4 = 32 = 2^5, and added the exponents, 4 + 3 = 7, so I got 2^(5 times 7) = 2^35.
I multiplied the bases to get 32 = 2^5 and multiplied the exponents to get 12, so I got 2^(5 times 12) = 2^60.
I rewrote 8^4 = 2^12 and 4^3 = 2^6 correctly, but then multiplied the exponents 12 and 6 instead of adding them.

hints: A power of a power multiplies exponents, and a product of powers of the same base adds exponents.

solutions.elegant: Count factors of $2$: each $8$ contributes three $2$s and each $4$ contributes two, so there are $4 \cdot 3 + 3 \cdot 2 = 18$ twos in the product.
